title: A common accessibility and compactness cardinal for a small family
statement: Use the universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U\prime$, smallness, accessibility and $\kappa$-compactness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and quasicategories and coherent mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be an accessible infinity category. Let $J$ be a $\mathcal U$-small set and let $(X_j)_{j\in J}$ be a family of objects of $\mathcal C$. There exists an infinite regular cardinal $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ such that $\mathcal C$ is $\kappa$-accessible and every $X_j$ is $\kappa$-compact in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9 and Corollary 5.3.4.15, small-family consequence (choose a sufficiently large sharply larger cardinal, not an arbitrary larger regular cardinal). Read online; not archived in literature/. No matching Stacks tag for this infinity-categorical assertion.

proof.text: Unpack accessibility: choose an infinite regular $\lambda\in\mathcal U$ such that $\mathcal C$ is $\lambda$-accessible, with an essentially small full family $G$ of $\lambda$-compact generators. For each $j\in J$, choose a small $\lambda$-filtered quasicategory $I_j$, a coherent diagram $p_j:I_j\to\mathcal C$ taking values in $G$, and a colimiting cocone with apex $X_j$. These choices are precisely the generation clause in the definition; they assert no colimits of arbitrary shapes in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.2(3), the accessibility convention in the cited definition; small-family application of the presentations used in the proof of Proposition 5.4.2.9.

proof.text: For each $j$ let $S_j$ be the set of nondegenerate simplices of $I_j$. It is $\mathcal U$-small because $I_j$ is small. Apply the small-family regular-bound lemma to the family indexed by $J\amalg\{*\}$ with fibers $S_j$ and the underlying set of the cardinal $\lambda$ at $*$. Obtain an infinite regular $\theta\in\mathcal U$ strictly larger than the cardinality of their disjoint union. In particular $\lambda<\theta$ and $|S_j|<\theta$ for every $j$, including when $J$ is empty.

source.place: Small-family size bound for the presentations in Proposition 5.4.2.9 and Corollary 5.3.4.15; explicit application of the cited set-theoretic lemma.

proof.text:
Set $a=2^	heta$ and $\kappa=a^+$, the successor cardinal. These belong to $\mathcal U$ by closure of a universe under power sets and small cardinal successors. By [lem-coef-infinite-cardinal-successor-regular] applied to the infinite cardinal $a$, the cardinal $\kappa$ is infinite regular (a union of fewer than $a^+$ sets of size less than $a^+$ has size at most $a\cdot a=a<a^+$). By [lem-coef-infinite-cardinal-square-power], $	heta<2^	heta$ and $(2^	heta)^	heta=2^	heta$. For $\mu<\kappa$ and $
u<\lambda<	heta$ we have $\mu\leq 2^	heta$ by the definition of successor cardinal and $
u\leq	heta$, so $\mu^
u\leq(2^	heta)^	heta=2^	heta<\kappa$; for $\mu=0$ the power is $0$ or $1$, still less than $\kappa$. Thus $\lambda<	heta<\kappa$ and the precise sharpness inequality holds; also every $I_j$ is $\kappa$-small since $|S_j|<	heta<\kappa$. This supplies a specific cardinal, rather than assuming that any larger regular cardinal works.

source.place: Definition A.2.6.3 and the subsequent successor-power example, printed p. 819; elementary cardinal arithmetic, with regularity and size inequalities written out.

proof.text: Apply the sharp accessibility-enlargement lemma to the $\lambda$-accessible category $\mathcal C$ from step 1 and the infinite regular cardinals $\lambda<\kappa$ from step 3. Its hypothesis $\mu^\nu<\kappa$ for $\mu<\kappa$, $\nu<\lambda$ is exactly the inequality established there. It follows that $\mathcal C$ is $\kappa$-accessible, in particular locally small and admitting all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits.

Every object $g$ of $G$ is $\kappa$-compact. Let $F:I\to\mathcal C$ be any small $\kappa$-filtered coherent diagram, and let $\eta:F\to\Delta_I L$ be any colimiting cocone. The indexing quasicategory $I$ is $\lambda$-filtered: every $\lambda$-small simplicial test diagram is $\kappa$-small, so its cocone exists by $\kappa$-filteredness. All such diagrams have colimits by $\lambda$-accessibility. By $\lambda$-compactness, the covariant corepresented coherent functor $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(g,-)$ sends this very cocone $\eta$ to a colimiting cocone in the specified infinity category of spaces, with components $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(g,F(i))\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(g,L)$. Since $F$ and $\eta$ were arbitrary, this is exactly preservation of every small $\kappa$-filtered colimiting cocone, hence the updated definition of $\kappa$-compactness. No assertion about changing the generating family is needed here.

source.place: Definition 5.3.4.5; monotonicity of compactness by restriction of the class of filtered diagrams.

proof.text: Fix $j\in J$. The diagram $p_j:I_j\to\mathcal C$ is $\kappa$-small by step 3; each of its vertices is $\kappa$-compact by step 5. The category $\mathcal C$ is locally small and admits all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by step 4, and the colimit of this particular diagram exists with apex $X_j$ by step 1. The compact-small-colimits lemma consequently makes $X_j$ $\kappa$-compact. This holds for every $j$, simultaneously for the single $\kappa$ of step 3, and step 4 gives the required accessibility at that same cardinal.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.15, printed p. 401, applied to the pre-existing filtered presentations; no cocompleteness hypothesis is used.

proof_origin.place: Explicit small-family assembly of the online Proposition 5.4.2.9 and Corollary 5.3.4.15; cardinal construction from the observation after Definition A.2.6.3. HTT is not archived in literature/: see WANTED in report.md.
